newsitem.title: UK: Palladium hits fresh low, gold awaits IMF meeting.
newsitem.headline: Palladium hits fresh low, gold awaits IMF meeting.

text.p: Palladium edged lower on Wednesday afternoon, fixing at a fresh 1993 low, while gold crept higher.

But dealers said gold was unlikely to make any significant move until after Friday's International Monetary Fund (IMF) meeting, which will discuss a plan to sell some IMF bullion reserves to aid poor nations.
"It's not going to go too far one way or the other until there's an decision on Friday to the IMF gold," one dealer said.
Gold fixed slightly higher at $383.50 per ounce after $383.15 in the morning and $383.10 on Tuesday afternoon.
So far spot gold has held in a tight range, with bids quoted from $383.90 to $382.80.
Analysts say U.S. investment funds have taken advantage of weak technicals and uncertainty regarding IMF sales to push down the gold market.

"Most of the action seems to be funds on the speculative short side trading off the market's fears -- be they unfounded or otherwise -- over the outcome of the IMF meeting on Friday," said Rhona O'Connell, metals analyst at T. Hoare and Company.
Open interest on Comex increased by nearly 12,000 lots on Monday, indicating the presence of large new short positions.
Whatever the outcome of the IMF meeting, prices are likely to see at least a brief short-covering bounce when the news is released, one dealer said.
Sickly palladium notched up a fresh low fixing in the afternoon at $122.25 per ounce, the weakest since December 1, 1993. The morning fix at 75 cents higher was the lowest since December 29, 1993.

Fund selling and long liquidation was responsible for the latest dips, but prices have been declining for months, under pressure from steady Russian sales and sluggish Japanese electronics demand, analysts said.
Spot prices so far have been locked in a narrow range, with bids quoted from $122.75 and $121.50.
One trader said an analysis of the weekly charts pointed to further losses down to $110 per ounce.
Platinum was also trapped in a narrow range, with bids seen between $392.30 and $393.00.
The market had been in a downtrend since early July but some chartists say the market moving towards oversold territory and expect a bounce soon.
